question: What is the first step when migrating a legacy codebase with an agent?

options.text: Start the migration immediately — the agent will figure it out
options.explanation: Without reconnaissance, the agent doesn't understand the scope, dependencies, and problem areas. The result will be chaotic

options.text: Reconnaissance in plan mode: analyze structure, dependencies, and problem areas
options.explanation: Plan mode lets you understand the current state without making changes. This is the foundation for a migration strategy

options.text: Write 50 skills for all possible transformations
options.explanation: Skills should be created after reconnaissance, when you know which transformations are common. Otherwise most skills will be useless

options.text: Delete the old code and write from scratch
options.explanation: Rewriting from scratch is one of the riskiest approaches in development. Step-by-step migration is safer and more predictable

question: Why describe both current (legacy) and target architecture in CLAUDE.md during migration?

options.text: For documentation — so the team knows the project history
options.explanation: Documentation is a side effect. The main reason — the agent needs to understand where (legacy) and where to (target) to migrate

options.text: The agent needs to know what patterns to transform from (current) and to (target)
options.explanation: Without legacy description the agent won't understand the current code. Without target description — it won't know what the result should look like

options.text: Claude Code requires both descriptions to work
options.explanation: There's no technical requirement. But without both architectures, the agent can't perform a meaningful migration

options.text: It's only needed for reporting to management
options.explanation: CLAUDE.md is a tool for the agent, not for management. Describing both architectures is critically important context

question: What does agent-friendly architecture mean in a greenfield project?

options.text: One module — one directory with predictable structure
options.explanation: The agent finds files by convention (users/users.controller.ts) rather than searching the entire project

options.text: Short files (up to 200 lines) that fit in context
options.explanation: A 2000-line file doesn't fit in context as a whole. The agent is forced to read in fragments and loses the big picture

options.text: All files in one directory for simplicity
options.explanation: A flat structure of 200 files is a nightmare for an agent. Module structure with predictable paths is much more efficient

options.text: Tests next to code — the agent sees code and tests simultaneously
options.explanation: When tests are in __tests__/ next to the module, the agent loads both code and tests and can keep them consistent

question: The agent works in user-service, but the task requires changes in order-service (different repository). What's the most effective solution?

options.text: Open a second terminal with Claude Code in order-service
options.explanation: Two independent agents don't coordinate with each other. Changes in user-service might be incompatible with order-service

options.text: CLAUDE.md with descriptions of all services + MCP server for cross-repo search
options.explanation: CLAUDE.md provides context about the entire system, MCP server allows searching code in other repos. The agent sees the full picture

options.text: Copy order-service code into user-service
options.explanation: This violates the repository separation principle and creates a synchronization problem

options.text: Abandon the microservice architecture
options.explanation: Architecture shouldn't be dictated by tool limitations. There are ways to work with multi-repo setups

question: How to run Claude Code in a CI/CD pipeline?

options.text: claude --mode auto — the agent will figure it out
options.explanation: auto mode in CI/CD is dangerous without strict limits. The -p flag (pipe mode) is specifically designed for non-interactive environments

options.text: claude -p 'task' — non-interactive mode via pipe
options.explanation: The -p flag runs the agent in non-interactive mode: it executes the task and exits. Ideal for CI/CD

options.text: claude --ci — special CI mode
options.explanation: No such flag exists. For CI/CD, the -p flag (pipe mode) is used

options.text: Claude Code can't be used in CI/CD
options.explanation: Claude Code works great in CI/CD via Agent SDK and the -p flag. This is one of the key use cases

question: Why is the anti-pattern 'the agent will handle everything' dangerous?

options.text: Without oversight, errors accumulate and make rollback harder
options.explanation: Each agent error affects subsequent steps. After 50 changes, finding and fixing a problem is like finding a needle in a haystack

options.text: The agent doesn't plan many steps ahead
options.explanation: The agent solves the current task. It doesn't see that the current solution will create problems 10 steps later

options.text: Context window is finite — the agent 'forgets' the start of a long session
options.explanation: During a long session, compaction occurs. The agent may lose important details and start contradicting earlier decisions

options.text: Claude Code disconnects after 100 operations
options.explanation: No such limit exists. The problem is the quality of the result, not a technical limit

question: You're starting a legacy migration. CLAUDE.md is ready, skills are created. What's next?

options.text: Run migration of all modules in parallel via sub-agents
options.explanation: Parallel migration creates conflicts: modules depend on each other, and parallel changes may be incompatible

options.text: Write tests for current behavior, then migrate one module at a time with test verification
options.explanation: Tests are a safety net. Without them you won't know if the agent broke anything. Step-by-step migration isolates problems

options.text: Migrate the most complex module first — if it works, the rest will be easier
options.explanation: Start with simple modules — refine the process. Migrate complex modules once you have experience and confidence in the skills

options.text: Ask the agent to rewrite everything from scratch on the target architecture
options.explanation: Rewriting from scratch is an anti-pattern. Step-by-step migration with tests is much safer

question: Which permission settings are critical for an agent in CI/CD?

options.text: deny: Write, Edit — the agent shouldn't modify files during code review
options.explanation: For code review and analysis tasks, the agent should only read. Write prohibition prevents accidental changes

options.text: deny: Bash(git push*) — the agent shouldn't push code
options.explanation: Pushing in CI/CD should be a controlled process. The agent shouldn't independently send changes

options.text: allow: Bash(*) — there's no user for confirmations in CI/CD
options.explanation: Bash(*) in CI/CD is maximally dangerous. The agent gets unlimited permissions without human oversight

options.text: disableBypassPermissionsMode: disable
options.explanation: In CI/CD nobody should be able to disable all security checks

question: A project has used Claude Code for 6 months. CLAUDE.md hasn't been updated. The architecture changed (switched from REST to GraphQL). What will happen?

options.text: The agent will automatically adapt to the new architecture
options.explanation: The agent follows instructions from CLAUDE.md. If REST is described there, it will generate REST endpoints in a GraphQL project

options.text: The agent will generate code using outdated patterns from CLAUDE.md
options.explanation: CLAUDE.md is the main source of rules. Outdated rules lead to generating code incompatible with the current architecture

options.text: Claude Code will issue a mismatch warning
options.explanation: Claude Code doesn't automatically compare CLAUDE.md with actual code. If CLAUDE.md says REST — the agent will do REST

options.text: Nothing changes — the agent ignores CLAUDE.md
options.explanation: CLAUDE.md is a key source of context. The agent actively uses it for decision-making

question: What minimum checklist must be completed before starting agent-based development?

options.text: CLAUDE.md describing stack, architecture, and conventions
options.explanation: Without CLAUDE.md the agent doesn't know project standards and will generate code at its discretion

options.text: .claude/settings.json with allow/deny
options.explanation: Without configured permissions the agent either asks for confirmation on every action or has too much freedom

options.text: At least smoke tests
options.explanation: Without tests it's impossible to verify whether the agent broke existing functionality

options.text: 50+ skills for all project tasks
options.explanation: 50 skills is excessive for a start. Begin with CLAUDE.md and basic settings, add skills as recurring tasks are identified

question: Cost of automated code review per PR via Claude Code: small PR ~$0.10, large PR ~$3.00. You have 50 PRs per day. What should you configure?

options.text: Nothing — $5-150/day is normal cost
options.explanation: Without monitoring, costs can grow unnoticed. Monitoring and limits are mandatory practice for CI/CD with agents

options.text: Cost monitoring and limits via --max-cost
options.explanation: Cost limit per run prevents unexpected expenses. Monitoring allows optimization — e.g., running full review only for large PRs

options.text: Disable code review — too expensive
options.explanation: Automated review pays off by catching bugs before merge. You should optimize, not disable

options.text: Run review only on Mondays
options.explanation: Bugs in PRs merged without review Tuesday-Friday will cost more than the daily automated review

question: Why is the context window a limiting factor for large tasks?

options.text: Claude Code limits sessions by time
options.explanation: The limitation isn't time-based but context volume. A long session with many messages fills the context window

options.text: When context fills, compaction occurs — the agent loses details from early steps and may contradict itself
options.explanation: Compaction compresses history to free space. The agent may lose important decisions from the start of the session

options.text: Context is infinite, the problem is model speed
options.explanation: The context window is finite. When it fills, compaction occurs — this is the main limitation for long tasks

options.text: The problem is only the cost of long sessions
options.explanation: Cost is a factor, but the main problem is context loss and quality degradation during compaction

question: You have a multi-repo of 12 microservices. How to ensure unified code standards across all repos?

options.text: Shared standards repository, copied to each repo via CI
options.explanation: A centralized source of rules (.claude/rules/, CLAUDE.md) syncs automatically — all repos get the same standards

options.text: CLAUDE.md with descriptions of all services and their interactions in each repo
options.explanation: The agent in each repo sees the full system picture: which services exist, how they interact, what API contracts there are

options.text: One CLAUDE.md for the entire organization in Confluence
options.explanation: Claude Code reads CLAUDE.md from the project filesystem, not from Confluence. Standards must be in the repository

options.text: Shared .claude/rules/ identical across all repos
options.explanation: Path-specific rules (backend, frontend, testing) can be shared across all repos — unified coding standards

question: You're launching a greenfield project. In what order should you configure Claude Code tools?

options.text: Skills → Hooks → CLAUDE.md → Settings
options.explanation: Skills and hooks are advanced tools. Start with the foundation: CLAUDE.md and settings

options.text: CLAUDE.md → Settings → Rules → Skills (as needed)
options.explanation: CLAUDE.md — foundation (stack, conventions). Settings — security. Rules — details for different project parts. Skills — as recurring tasks are identified

options.text: Settings → Managed policy → Plugins → CLAUDE.md
options.explanation: Managed policy and plugins are enterprise-level. For a new project, start with CLAUDE.md and basic settings

options.text: Order doesn't matter — configure in any order
options.explanation: Order matters: without CLAUDE.md the agent doesn't know standards, without settings — too much or too little freedom. Foundation first
